newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index up 0.5 pct at 292.02.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index up 0.5 pct at 292.02.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation composite investable index IFC/IPRD, denominated in dollars, rose 0.5 percent to 292.02 on Wednesday.
Latin America edged up 1.3 percent day-on-day to 528.98, Asia was down 0.3 percent at 249.83, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.8 percent at 135.07.
The IFC composite index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index BFFO, also denominated in dollars, was up 0.67 percent day-on-day at 158.31 at 1449 GMT.
The year's high was 165.948, reached on July 3. It touched the year's 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index .CEMF=USD, was up 0.55 percent at 475.069, calculated after the close of play on Tuesday.
It touched a 1996 high at 505.452 on July 4; the year's 458.369 low was recorded on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns from 22 emerging market nations. Changes are reported with one day's lag at 1300 GMT.

The J.P. Morgan emerging market local currency index ELMI, in dollar terms, rose 0.04 percent to 121.41 on Wednesday. By region, Latin America was down 0.12 percent to 98.05, Asia rose 0.04 percent to 128.42, and East Europe was up 0.22 at 160.35. --Julia Meehan, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
